newsitem.title: FRANCE: Successor to jailed French minister investigated.
newsitem.headline: Successor to jailed French minister investigated.

text.p: The man filling in for jailed ex-communications minister Alain Carignon as president of the regional council of Isere in the French Alps was himself placed under investigation on Friday for alleged corruption.

Gaullist Michel Hannoun told a news conference that he was suspected of receiving several hundreds of thousands of francs (tens of thousands of dollars) in fees for fictitious consultancy work from 1989 to 1992.
Hannoun, who is also a deputy in the National Assembly and mayor of the small town of Voreppe near the Alpine city of Grenoble, said he would not resign from the regional council.
Hannoun denied wrongdoing, saying he had been paid as a professional consultant for work which included various unspecified studies and reports.

An appeal court in Lyon sentenced Carignon in July to four years in prison, with another year suspended, for taking 21 million francs ($4 million) in gifts from utilities giant Lyonnaise des Eaux in return for a water privatisation contract when he was mayor of Grenoble. He was also banned from public office for five years
